headline: RBI's $239 bn forward dollar position to limit rupee gains: Report
summary:
The Reserve Bank of India's net short position of USD 239 billion in the forward market is likely to limit the rupee's appreciation despite a recovery in foreign portfolio investor (FPI) inflows, according to a report.
The Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) forward book stood at a net dollar short position of USD 239 billion as of September 2026, reflecting its commitment to provide dollars when buy-sell swaps mature. This will require the central bank to accumulate dollars as capital inflows improve, limiting the rupee's appreciation, IDFC First Bank Economic Research report said.
Around USD 40 billion of the short position matures within a year, USD 56 billion in one to three years and the remaining USD 143 billion in three to five years. The longer-duration positions are largely linked to the FCNR (B) scheme, it added.

headline: Rupee among Asia's top performing currencies as AI trade cools
summary: The Indian rupee has gained considerable strength in FY27, aided by increased foreign portfolio investor inflows. A notable decline in crude oil prices has also positively impacted the rupee's performance. Experts believe the Reserve Bank of India will manage the currency's appreciation to rebuild its foreign exchange reserves. Recent interventions in the currency market have capped further gains in the rupee.

headline: RBI's $239 bn forward dollar position to limit rupee gains despite FPI inflows: Report
summary: The Reserve Bank of India currently has a net short position of USD 239 billion in the forward market, which may hinder the rupee's ability to strengthen, even as foreign portfolio investor inflows improve. This influx could potentially be managed by the Reserve Bank, capping any gains for the rupee against the US dollar.
